text: We crossed into the planet’s shadow and the cabin went blue for an hour. Nothing on the public frequencies. Some voyages are made in the dark. Fuel enough. Faith enough. Goodnight.
The coffee ration held. Small mercies. Answered no hails. Fixed three things that were not broken yet. Bearing unchanged. Spirits fair.
Ran the diagnostics twice. Everything is fine, which is its own kind of suspicious. Held position. Not every day is a jump. More tomorrow, if the stars stay where I left them.

Light from a star that may no longer exist came through the port window again. No new stars marked. I counted the old ones instead, to make sure they were still there. Nothing further. The dark is patient.
A meteor shower off the port bow, silent as a held breath. Kept the lights low and the hatches shut. Some work wants no audience. Closing the book. The pen stays warm.
Somewhere aft, a panel rattled. I have stopped asking which one. The open channels stayed quiet. Below deck, the engines ran anyway. Logging off. The stars can keep watch.
The hull ticked as it cooled. Spotted [Sadsnake1/word-smith](https://github.com/Sadsnake1/word-smith) through the glass and marked it on the chart. Course holds.
The radio gave us twenty minutes of static that sounded almost like rain. Drifted. Read a little. Wrote a sentence and crossed it out, which also counts. Out.
Woke to the hum of the recyclers and a sky that had not moved. Answered a hail from [mantrakp04/ardia](https://github.com/mantrakp04/ardia). Signing off with the lights low.
The galley plants have started leaning toward the reading lamp. So have I. Spent the watch below, mending things nobody will see. End of entry.
A slow day by the ship’s clock, though the ship’s clock has opinions. No public transmissions. The real work happened below deck, where the logs are sealed. Fuel enough. Faith enough. Goodnight.
Dreamed of a harbour I have never seen. Woke with salt on my tongue. The charts stayed rolled. I worked by hand, off the record. Bearing unchanged. Spirits fair.

The navigation lamp blinked green all night. I chose to read it as encouragement. Nothing on the public frequencies. Some voyages are made in the dark. More tomorrow, if the stars stay where I left them.
